claims.claim: Celestica is positioned in the physical AI-infrastructure chain through networking/server hardware manufacturing; the causal thesis depends on sustained hyperscale capex, outsourced manufacturing content and continued favorable mix rather than on AI demand alone.
The principal successor bottlenecks are customer concentration, program execution, component availability and the ability to retain content if customers insource or redesign platforms.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Current primary evidence supports participation in fast-growing networking/server infrastructure, but not exclusive control of the bottleneck.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Demand can remain strong across AI buildout scenarios, while customer insourcing, program loss or capex normalization can break the company-specific transmission.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Manufacturing capability is useful across platform generations, but customer redesign and alternate manufacturers remain substitutes.

risks.risk: AI infrastructure demand can persist while Celestica captures less value if customers insource, redesign platforms or shift programs to competing manufacturers.

causalEdges.mechanism: larger clusters require more physical compute and network hardware
causalEdges.falsifier: hyperscale capex or deployed hardware volumes materially contract

causalEdges.mechanism: outsourced platform manufacturing converts customer deployments into Celestica revenue
causalEdges.falsifier: customers insource, redesign away Celestica content, or transfer major programs

causalEdges.from: higher program volume and favorable mix
causalEdges.mechanism: factory absorption and mix can expand margins
causalEdges.falsifier: margin expansion reverses despite sustained revenue growth

unknowns.unknown: Customer-specific concentration, program duration and unit economics remain unquantified in the reviewed cumulative evidence.

claims.claim: The current evidence does not falsify the growth thesis: Q2 revenue, margin and EPS all improved materially, but rapid growth raises concentration, execution and expectation risk.
No defensible evidence in the reviewed packet establishes unusual financing/dilution or governance stress; those dimensions remain unasserted rather than presumed benign or bearish.

factors.name: thesisQuality
factors.basis: Operating evidence is strong, while customer/program concentration and competitive substitution are not quantified.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Reviewed evidence does not establish component concentration or alternate-source resilience.

risks.risk: Large customer programs can create revenue concentration and abrupt downside if a platform is delayed, lost or insourced.
Raised guidance and rapid margin expansion increase sensitivity to normalization, unfavorable mix or execution slippage.
AI TAM growth is not equivalent to durable Celestica pricing power or share retention.

causalEdges.mechanism: large program changes can reduce volume faster than fixed capacity adjusts
causalEdges.falsifier: diversification rises while utilization and margins remain resilient through program transitions

unknowns.unknown: Exact top-customer exposure and program economics are not established by the reviewed evidence.
No source-addressed current financing/dilution or governance assessment is present in the reviewed Beta inputs.
